1. Objective

The objective of this Anti-Bribery & Anti-Corruption Policy is to establish a framework for ethical, fair, and lawful business practices and to prevent bribery, corruption, fraud, unethical payments, undue advantages, and improper business conduct in all operations of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. in compliance with applicable laws including the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended), Companies Act, 2013, Prevention of Money Laundering Act, and other applicable legal, regulatory, and ethical standards.

2. Scope

This Anti-Bribery & Anti-Corruption Policy applies to all employees, trainees, contractual staff, consultants, technical personnel, vendors, suppliers, contractors, agents, intermediaries, business associates, and any other individuals or entities acting for or on behalf of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

3. Policy

The Company prohibits all forms of bribery and corruption in its business dealings. No employee, director, consultant, contractor, vendor, agent, or representative acting on behalf of the Company shall directly or indirectly offer, give, promise, request, receive, or accept any bribe, kickback, improper payment, favor, gift, or other benefit intended to influence a business decision or secure an unfair advantage.

Prohibited Conduct

Employees and representatives of the Company shall not:

  • Offer or accept bribes, kickbacks, commissions, or unlawful payments.
  • Make or authorize facilitation payments, speed money, or unofficial payments to government officials or any other person.
  • Use their position for personal gain or to provide undue advantage to others.
  • Engage in fraudulent, dishonest, or unethical business practices.
  • Falsify financial records, invoices, expenses, or supporting documentation.

Gifts and Hospitality

Reasonable business gifts, hospitality, or promotional items of nominal value may be exchanged only when they are lawful, infrequent, transparent, and do not influence business decisions or create a conflict of interest.

Cash gifts or cash equivalents are strictly prohibited.

Accurate Records

All business transactions must be accurately recorded and supported by proper documentation. Employees must ensure that Company records are complete, truthful, and maintained in accordance with applicable laws and Company procedures.

Reporting Concerns

Employees must promptly report any suspected or actual violation of this policy to the directors.

The Company will investigate all reported concerns appropriately and confidentially.

Protection Against Retaliation

No employee shall be subjected to retaliation, discrimination, or adverse action for reporting a concern in good faith or participating in an investigation.

Compliance

All employees are required to comply with this policy and applicable laws, including the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended), the Companies Act, 2013, and other relevant anti-corruption and anti-fraud regulations.

Responsibility

Every employee is responsible for maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct and ensuring that business activities are conducted honestly, fairly, and in the best interests of the Company.

Non-Compliance, Investigation and Disciplinary Action:

The Company reserves the right to investigate any suspected or reported violation and take appropriate disciplinary action, which may include:

  • Written warning or reprimand
  • Suspension from duties
  • Recovery of financial losses or damages
  • Termination of employment or contractual engagement
  • Blacklisting of vendors, suppliers, contractors, consultants, or business partners
  • Reporting the matter to regulatory or law enforcement authorities
  • Initiation of civil or criminal legal proceedings, where applicable

Disciplinary action shall be determined based on the nature and severity of the violation and will be taken in accordance with Company policies, applicable laws, and relevant statutory provisions, including the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended), the Companies Act, 2013, and other applicable anti-corruption, anti-fraud, and commercial laws.

3. Exceptions

All exceptions and deviations to this policy will require the approval of all the directors.

3. Effective Date

This policy will come into effect from 30th June 2026. The Company reserves the right to review, interpret, modify, or amend this policy in accordance with legal, operational, and compliance requirements.

1. Objective

The objective of this Asset Issuance & Return Policy is to establish a structured framework for the issuance, usage, protection, tracking, maintenance, and return of Company assets issued to employees and associated personnel of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

2. Scope

This Asset Issuance & Return Policy applies to all employees and authorized users who are issued, assigned, authorized to use, or responsible for any Company-owned asset or operational resource of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

3. Policy

  • All Company assets including laptops, desktops, mobile phones, ID cards, access cards, PPE kits, uniforms, tools, machinery accessories, storage devices, software, technical instruments, documents, communication devices, operational equipment, and other resources issued to employees shall remain the sole property of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.
  • Employees receiving Company assets shall acknowledge receipt of the assets and may be required to sign asset issuance records prescribed by the Company.
  • Employees shall use Company assets strictly for authorized official purposes and in a safe, responsible, lawful, professional, and operationally appropriate manner.
  • Employees shall not sell, transfer, lend, lease, modify, tamper with, duplicate, misuse, dispose of, or allow unauthorized persons to use Company assets without prior approval from authorized Company personnel.
  • Employees using safety equipment shall comply with all applicable operational instructions, safety procedures and usage guidelines.
  • Any loss shall be immediately reported to the authorized personnel.
  • Employees shall immediately return all Company assets upon resignation or whenever directed by the management.
  • Assets returned by employees shall be subject to physical verification, operational inspection, inventory review, condition assessment, and clearance procedures as prescribed by the Company.
  • Recovery of repair cost, replacement cost, or non-return of Company assets may be made in accordance with Company policy, employment terms, and applicable laws.
  • Company data and confidential information stored within Company assets shall remain the property of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. and shall be protected in accordance with Company policies.
  • Employees shall not install unauthorized software, remove security controls, alter asset identification labels, disable tracking systems, or modify Company-issued devices or equipment without approval.
  • Periodic physical verification of Company assets may be conducted by authorized personnel.
  • Normal wear and tear arising from authorized and reasonable use of Company assets during the course of official duties shall not ordinarily attract recovery or disciplinary action subject to verification by the Company.

3. Exceptions

All exceptions and deviations to this policy will require the approval of all the directors.

5. Effective Date

This policy will come into effect from 30th June 2026. The Company reserves the right to review, interpret, modify, or amend this policy in accordance with legal, operational, and compliance requirements.

1. Objective

The objective of this Attendance and Late Coming Policy is to establish clear standards regarding employee attendance and punctuality in order to maintain workplace discipline and smooth functioning of business operations at Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

2. Scope

This Attendance and Late Coming Policy apply to all employees of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd..

3. Policy

Regular attendance and punctuality are essential for the smooth functioning of the Company. All employees are expected to report to work on time, follow their assigned work schedules, and comply with attendance procedures.

Working Hours

  • Standard working hours are 8:55 AM to 6:00 PM.
  • Employees are required to complete 9 hours of work per day, including the 60 min lunch/tea break.
  • The Company may record attendance through any approved attendance management system.

Attendance Requirements

  • Employees must report to duty on time and remain present during their scheduled working hours.
  • In case of delay, absence, emergency, or inability to report to work, employees must inform their Reporting Manager or HR Department as early as possible.
  • Leaving the workplace during working hours without approval is not permitted.

Late Coming

  • A grace period of 10 minutes is allowed after the start of working hours.
  • Employees reporting after 9:05 AM will be marked as Late Coming.
  • Repeated late reporting is discouraged and may result in corrective or disciplinary action.

Consequences of Late Coming

  • Three (3) late marks in a month will result in half-day salary deduction and 5 late marks for full day salary deduction.
  • Additional late marks may lead to further salary deductions as per the Company's payroll rules.
  • Habitual late coming may also result in verbal counselling, written warnings, or other disciplinary action.

Absence and Attendance Violations

The following may be treated as misconduct:

  • Unauthorized absence from work.
  • Failure to record attendance.
  • Leaving the workplace without permission.
  • Repeated late coming or violation of attendance procedures.
  • Misrepresentation of attendance records.

Such cases may attract disciplinary action in accordance with Company policy.

Breaks

  • Employees are entitled to authorized lunch, tea, and rest breaks as prescribed by the Company.
  • Reasonable personal and biological breaks are permitted.
  • Misuse of break time or excessive absence from the workstation may result in disciplinary action.

Management Rights

The Company reserves the right to review attendance records periodically and take appropriate corrective or disciplinary action based on attendance performance, operational requirements, and applicable laws.

Attendance Record Tampering

Tampering with attendance records, biometric systems, proxy attendance, or unauthorized marking of attendance for another employee shall be treated as serious misconduct and may invite disciplinary action.

Overtime & Shift Extension

Employees may be required to work overtime, extended shifts, or additional working hours based on operational requirements, production schedules, maintenance activities, emergency situations, or management instructions subject to applicable laws and Company procedures.

4. Exception

Exceptions relating to attendance, late coming, shift timings, leave, emergency absence, medical situations, operational requirements, machine breakdown, travel delays, project assignments, field work, or other exceptional circumstances may be considered by the Management. All exceptions and deviations to this policy will require the approval of all the directors.

5. Effective Date

This policy will come into effect from 30th June 2026. Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. reserves the right to review and amend any provision of this policy in accordance with operational needs, workforce requirements, safety considerations, and applicable laws.

1. Objective

The objective of the Code of Conduct policy of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. is to define clear standards of ethical behavior, professionalism, and integrity expected from all employees while performing their duties.

2. Scope

This policy and procedure apply to all departments and employees of the Organization.

3. Policy

1. Our Commitment

Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. is committed to conducting its business with fairness, transparency, honesty, integrity, and the highest ethical standards. All employees are expected to follow this Code of Conduct in letter and spirit.

2. General Standards of Conduct

All employees must:

  • Act honestly, fairly, professionally, and responsibly in all business dealings.
  • Follow all Company policies, procedures, rules, and instructions.
  • Respect the Company’s reputation and act in a manner that upholds its image.
  • Raise concerns or suggestions regarding policies through proper internal channels rather than violating them.
  • Employees are expected to maintain discipline, professionalism, and accountability in all work-related activities.

3. Equal Opportunity & Respect at Workplace

The Company provides equal opportunity to all employees.

  • No discrimination is allowed based on age, gender, caste, religion, race, nationality, marital status, disability, sexual orientation, or personal beliefs.
  • All employees must treat colleagues, customers, vendors, and visitors with respect and dignity.
  • A respectful, inclusive, and harassment-free workplace must be maintained at all times.

4. Dual Employment or Outside Business Activity

  • Employees are prohibited from engaging in any other employment, whether full-time, part-time, contractual, freelance, consulting, or similar work arrangement with any other company, organization, or individual during the course of their employment with the Company, unless prior written approval has been obtained from the Company.
  • Employees are also not permitted to start, operate, participate in, or associate with any personal business, startup, venture, partnership, or commercial activity without formally informing the Company in writing.
  • The Company reserves the right to review and approve or reject such requests based on business interests, conflict of interest considerations, confidentiality obligations, employee performance, and applicable legal or contractual requirements.
  • Failure to disclose external employment or business involvement, or engaging in unauthorized dual employment or outside business activity, may result in disciplinary and legal action, including termination of employment.

5. Positive Work Environment & Teamwork

  • Employees are expected to work collaboratively as a team.
  • Mutual respect, open communication, and knowledge sharing are encouraged.
  • Employees should support each other’s development and contribute to a healthy and productive work culture.
  • Personal interests must not override team or Company interests.

6. Conflict of Interest

A conflict of interest arises when personal interests interfere with Company interests.

Employees must:

  • Avoid any situation where personal, family, or financial interests conflict with Company duties.
  • Not be involved in decision-making where relatives or close associates are employed or have business interest.
  • Not use Company position, information, or resources for personal gain.
  • Disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest immediately to the HR Department in writing.

If unsure, employees must consult their Manager or HR before taking action.

  • Use of office address or official email ID for personal courier deliveries is not allowed. Employees are requested to use their personal address and personal contact details for any non-business shipments.

7. Use of Company Assets

  • Company assets (machines, tools, vehicles, computers, documents, equipment, etc.) must be used only for official purposes.
  • Employees must protect Company property from misuse, damage, loss, theft, or unauthorized use.
  • Company assets must not be shared, loaned, sold, or used for personal benefit without approval.

8. Attendance & Punctuality

  • Employees are expected to maintain regular attendance and punctuality.
  • Any late coming, early leaving, or absence must be pre-approved by the Reporting Manager.
  • Unauthorized absence or repeated delays may lead to disciplinary action.

9. Drugs, Alcohol & Intoxicants

  • The use, possession, or distribution of alcohol, drugs, or any intoxicating substance is strictly prohibited within Company premises.
  • Employees must not report to work or perform duties under the influence of such substances.
  • This rule applies to all Company locations, client sites, travel, and Company-sponsored events.

10. Confidentiality & Information Protection

Employees must:

  • Keep all Company information strictly confidential, including technical data, designs, drawings, business plans, financial details, customer and vendor information, and internal records.
  • Not share confidential information with unauthorized persons or external parties.
  • Not disclose Company information to media, public platforms, or external agencies without approval from Management.
  • Use Company information only for legitimate business purposes.

11. Reporting Concerns

Employees are encouraged to report:

  • Any unethical behaviour
  • Policy violations
  • Conflicts of interest
  • Safety or security concerns

Reports should be made to the Reporting Manager or HR Department without fear of retaliation.

12. Compliance

Failure to comply with this Code of Conduct may result in disciplinary action, including warning, suspension, or termination of employment depending on the seriousness of the violation.

All employees are required to follow applicable laws, regulations, and Company policies at all times.

3. Exceptions

All exceptions and deviations to this policy will require the approval of all the directors.

3. Effective Date

This policy will come into effect from 30th June 2026. The Company reserves the right to review, interpret, modify, or amend this policy in accordance with legal, operational, and compliance requirements.

1. Objective

The objective of this Confirmation Policy is to establish a fair and structured process for assessing the performance, conduct, competency and overall suitability of employees during the probation period and confirming their employment with Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. upon satisfactory completion of prescribed requirements.

2. Scope

This policy and procedure apply to all departments and employees of the Organization.

3. Policy

  • All employees will be on probation for Eight months; this period may be altered by the management at its discretion. At the end of the probation period their services with the company would be confirmed, subject to their performance meeting the requisite standards.
  • Employee performance will be assessed on the basis of the role/responsibilities defined at the time of appointment.
  • Confirmation Process-

1. HR would ask the ‘Confirmation Mail’ from the reporting manager, 15 days prior to the date of confirmation.

2. Based on the reporting manager’s feedback, HR would move the confirmation process forward.

3. If an employee is confirmed, HR will have a discussion with the employee based on the reporting manager’s feedback, within 5 days of the date of confirmation.

4. Following the conversation, HR will hand over a letter of confirmation to the employee and file a copy of the same in the employee’s record.

5. If an employee is not confirmed or the probation period is extended, the reporting manager and the HR will have a discussion with the employee, conveying the reporting manager’s feedback, within 3 days of the date of confirmation.

6. Following the conversation, HR will draft a letter outlining the manager’s feedback and the employee’s comments from the discussion; a copy of this letter will be handed over to the employee and the original would be documented in the employee’s record for future review.

  • Note:

a) On confirmation there will be no change in annual cost to the company and other benefits. Confirmation itself does not trigger salary increase. Salary revisions governed by Pay & Incentives Policy.

b) While on probation, the employee will be required to serve 7 days’ notice period.

c) PIP will be applicable to the candidates in probation period.

  • Confidentiality:

In the confirmation process, the feedback and the discussion that ensued between different parties should be treated with utmost confidentiality. It is the responsibility of HR, the reporting manager (or her/his nominee) and the employee, to ensure this confidentiality.

3. Exceptions

All exceptions and deviations to this policy will require the approval of all the directors.

3. Effective Date

This policy will come into effect from 30th June 2026. The Company reserves the right to review, interpret, modify, or amend this policy in accordance with legal, operational, and compliance requirements.

1. Objective

The objective of this Data Privacy & Confidentiality Policy is to establish guidelines for the protection, handling, storage, usage, and disclosure of confidential, technical, operational, commercial, employee, customer, vendor, and business-related information of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

2. Scope

This Data Privacy & Confidentiality Policy applies to all employees of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

3. Policy

Confidentiality Policy

All employees of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. must keep all Company information strictly confidential.

What is Confidential Information

Confidential information includes, but is not limited to:

  • Technical drawings, designs, and manufacturing processes
  • Pricing, quotations, and commercial details
  • Customer, vendor, and employee information
  • Contracts and project details
  • Business plans, reports, and internal communications
  • Software, passwords, and system access details

Employee Responsibilities

  • Employees must not share Company information with anyone who is not authorized.
  • Confidential information must be used only for official work purposes.
  • Employees must take care to protect all Company information from loss, misuse, or unauthorized access.
  • Confidential documents must not be copied, printed, photographed, scanned, or shared without permission.
  • Passwords, login details, and access codes must be kept secure and must not be shared with others.
  • Confidentiality must be maintained at all times, including while working from home or outside the office.
  • Visitors, contractors, and outsiders must not be allowed access to sensitive Company information.
  • Confidential documents and files must be properly stored and never left unattended.

Data Security

  • Employees must immediately report any suspected data breach or security issue to the IT Department or management.
  • All intellectual property created during employment belongs to the Company.

Return of Company Information

  • All Company documents, devices, files, drawings, and access credentials must be returned when an employee resigns, is transferred, or leaves the Company, or when requested by management.

Post-Employment Confidentiality

  • Employees must continue to maintain confidentiality even after leaving the Company.

Disciplinary action:

  • Any actual or suspected data breach, confidentiality breach, or security incident must be reported immediately to the Reporting Manager, HR, IT Department, or authorized personnel.
  • The Company may take immediate action to control the situation, such as restricting access, securing systems, investigating the issue, and preventing further damage.
  • Employees must fully cooperate with any investigation. All incidents will be handled as per Company policies and applicable legal and cybersecurity requirements.

3. Exceptions

All exceptions and deviations to this policy will require the approval of all the directors.

3. Effective Date

This policy will come into effect from 30th June 2026. The Company reserves the right to review, interpret, modify, or amend this policy in accordance with legal, operational, and compliance requirements.

1. Objective

The objective of this Disciplinary Policy is to ensure a fair, consistent, and professional approach towards addressing employee misconduct, unsafe practices, and unsatisfactory performance within Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

2. Scope

This Policy applies to all employees of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

3. Policy

Any act, omission, negligence, violation of Company rules, unsafe practice, breach of duty, misconduct, or behavior inconsistent with the policies, operational procedures, safety standards, employment terms, or expected standards of conduct of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. shall be treated as misconduct and may invite disciplinary action as per Company policy.

  • The following acts or omissions on the part of an employee shall be treated as Minor Misconduct under the disciplinary policy of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

1. Reporting late to duty or leaving the workplace early, absence for less than Two consecutive days without proper approval.

2. Loitering, gossiping, unnecessary gathering, or causing disturbance during working hours.

3. Failure to wear prescribed uniform, safety equipment, identity card, or required dress code while on duty.

4.Failure to maintain cleanliness, discipline, or proper workplace behaviour within Company premises.

5. Non-compliance with routine instructions issued by supervisors, department heads, or authorized personnel.

6. Unauthorized use of mobile phones, personal devices, or engaging in non-work-related activities during working hours were restricted.

7. Minor violation of Company procedures, safety instructions, or operational guidelines.

8. Improper handling or careless use of Company tools, equipment, machinery, materials, or resources without causing major damage or loss.

  • PENALTIES FOR MINOR MISCONDUCT: Depending upon the nature and seriousness of the Minor Misconduct, Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. may take appropriate disciplinary action which may include verbal warning, written warning, counselling, adverse remarks in service records, recovery of loss or damage caused due to negligence, deduction of wages as permitted under applicable rules and laws, temporary suspension of certain workplace privileges, or any other corrective action considered appropriate by the management.
  • PROGRESSIVE DISCIPLINARY PROCESS in case of MINOR misconduct:

Progressive disciplinary action for Minor Misconduct at Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. shall normally follow a fair and corrective approach depending upon the nature and frequency of the misconduct:

1. The concerned employee shall be informed about the misconduct or behavioural concern at the earliest opportunity by the Reporting Manager. A lag here could imply your acceptance of poor performance or unacceptable behaviour.

2. The issue shall be discussed with the employee through formal or informal counselling to understand the reason leading to the misconduct. The employee shall be given a fair opportunity to present their response and clarify their position.

3. Based on the nature of the issue, corrective measures such as counselling, additional training, performance guidance, safety instruction, process clarification, closer supervision, or improvement targets may be provided to support corrective behaviour and operational improvement.

4. A reasonable review period may be provided to monitor improvement as applicable to the employee’s role and responsibilities.

5. Employees shall be informed about the consequences of repeated non-compliance or failure to improve, which may result in verbal warning, written warning, final warning, suspension, or further disciplinary action including review of employment by the management.

6. Documentation of the outcome.

I. The person should be allowed to see, sign and make any comments on this file note.

II. Concentrate on the facts of the situation and the clear quantifiable measurements to support these facts.

III. Ensure there is evidence for facts and figures.

The person should be allowed time to demonstrate improvement, in line with the standards set at the counselling meeting.

If the behaviour persists, act as per the notified consequences.

  • The following acts or omission on the part of an employee shall amount to MAJOR misconduct:

1. Wilful insubordination or refusal to follow lawful instructions issued by authorized supervisors or management.

2. Disobedience of Company rules, operational procedures, or safety instructions.

3. Participation in illegal strikes, stoppage of work, or disruption of Company operations.

4. Intentional slowing down of work, production, or operational activities.

5. Theft, fraud, dishonesty, or misappropriation of Company property, materials, or records.

6. Demanding, accepting, or offering bribes, illegal gratification, or unauthorized commission.

7. Habitual absence without leave or continuous absence from duty for more than four working days without approval.

8. Habitual violation of Company policies, standing orders, or workplace regulations.

9. Collection of money or conducting unauthorized trade or business activities within Company premises.

10. Reporting to duty under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or prohibited substances.

11. Fighting, threatening, abusive, violent, or disorderly behaviour within Company premises.

12. Wilful damage, misuse, or negligent handling of machinery, equipment, tools, vehicles, or Company assets.

13. Unauthorized operation of machinery, equipment, or technical systems.

14. Serious negligence resulting in accident, injury, safety risk, or operational loss.

15. Refusal to use prescribed safety equipment or violation of safety procedures.

16. Unauthorized disclosure or misuse of confidential Company information or documents.

17. Falsification of records, attendance, reports, documents, or Company information.

18. Harassment, intimidation, discrimination, or misconduct affecting workplace discipline and dignity.

19. Possession of unauthorized weapons, hazardous materials, or prohibited items within Company premises.

20. Sleeping during working hours while on duty, especially in operational or safety-sensitive areas causing major harm to the company.

21. Unauthorized entry into restricted, confidential, or operational areas of the Company.

22. Tampering with safety devices, machinery settings, electrical systems, or operational controls.

23. Refusal to cooperate during disciplinary inquiry, safety investigation, or official Company proceedings.

24. Misuse of Company identity, official position, authority, or organizational resources for personal benefit.

25. Any act or behaviour causing serious reputational, financial, operational, or safety-related harm to Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

26. Canvassing for union membership or collection of union funds within the premises of the establishment.
27. Holding meetings inside the premises of the establishment without the permission of the manager.
28. Smoking or spitting on the premises of the establishment, where it is prohibited.

  • The Company will normally adhere to the following PROGRESSIVE DISCIPLINARY PROCESS in case of major misconduct:

    1. Verbal Caution: An employee may be given a verbal caution (Reminder or informal heads up) for initial instances of misconduct, unsafe behaviour, operational negligence, indiscipline, or violation of Company procedures. The purpose of the verbal caution is to inform the employee about the issue and provide an opportunity for corrective improvement. The verbal caution shall be documented by the Supervisor, Department Head, or HR Department and may remain valid for a period of up to One month.

    2. Verbal Warning: A verbal warning is more serious than a verbal caution. An employee will be given a verbal warning when a problem is identified. Verbal warnings are documented and placed in the employee’s personnel file and will remain in effect for One month.

    3. Written Warning: A written warning is more serious than a verbal warning. Written warnings are maintained in an employee’s personnel file and remain in effect for three to six months based on the nature of the misconduct.

    4. Suspension: A suspension without pay is more serious than a written warning. An employee will be suspended when he or she engages in conduct that justifies a suspension or the employee engages in unacceptable behaviour during the period that a written warning is in effect. An employee's suspension will be documented and, regardless of the length of the suspension issued, will remain in effect for three months.

5.Decision Making Leave: Generally following a suspension, an employee will be reprimanded and sent home for the day on decision making leave. This is intended to help the employee decide whether they should continue employment with the company. If the employee returns, they will be expected to work harder than before to follow the Company guidelines and continue their employment without interruption. The other option with this leave is the employee may choose to resign because employment with the Company is not a match.

6. Termination: Employment may be terminated in cases involving serious misconduct, repeated violations, non-improvement despite disciplinary action, breach of safety standards, fraud, violence, theft, confidentiality breach, or conduct harmful to the interests of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. Termination proceedings shall be carried out in accordance with Company policies, applicable laws, and where required, in consultation with authorized legal or professional advisors.

3. Exceptions

All exceptions and deviations to this policy will require the approval of all the directors.

3. Effective Date

This policy will come into effect from 30th June 2026. The Company reserves the right to review, interpret, modify, or amend this policy in accordance with legal, operational, and compliance requirements.

1. Objective

The objective of this Equal Opportunity & Anti-Discrimination Policy is to promote a fair, inclusive, respectful, and discrimination-free workplace where all employees and associated personnel of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. are treated with dignity, equality, and professionalism in compliance with applicable laws including the Constitution of India, Equal Remuneration Act, 1976, Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, and other applicable labor and employment regulations.

2. Scope

This Equal Opportunity & Anti-Discrimination Policy applies to all employees.

3. Policy

Equal Opportunity & Anti-Discrimination Policy

Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. is committed to providing a fair, inclusive, respectful and equal opportunity workplace for all employees.

Equal Opportunity

  • All employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, skills, performance and business needs.
  • The Company does not discriminate against anyone based on gender, age, caste, religion, race, disability, marital status, pregnancy, language, region, political views, or any other protected characteristic.

Respectful Workplace

  • All employees must be treated with dignity, fairness, and respect.
  • The Company does not tolerate harassment, bullying, intimidation, victimization, abusive behaviour, or offensive conduct of any kind.
  • Sexual harassment is strictly prohibited and will be handled as per the applicable law, including the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

Employee Conduct

Employees must not:

  • Discriminate against others in any form
  • Use offensive language, jokes, or remarks
  • Engage in unfair or biased treatment
  • Exclude or humiliate others in the workplace
  • Create a hostile or uncomfortable work environment

Inclusive Workplace

The Company promotes a safe, healthy, and inclusive workplace for all employees, including shop-floor workers, technical staff, office staff, trainees, supervisors, and persons with disabilities.

Reporting Concerns

  • Employees are encouraged to report any discrimination, harassment, unfair treatment, or inappropriate behaviour.
  • Reports can be made to HR or authorized management personnel.
  • No employee will face retaliation for reporting concerns in good faith or participating in an investigation.

Awareness & Training

The Company may conduct training, awareness programs, and workplace behaviour initiatives to promote equality, inclusion, and respectful conduct.

Compliance with Law

The Company complies with all applicable laws, including:

  • Constitution of India
  • Equal Remuneration Act, 1976
  • Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
  • Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013

2. Scope

3. Policy

1. Retirement

Employees shall retire upon completing 58 years of age, or as per Company policy updated from time to time.

1 Notice Period

  • If waived, the employee may be required to pay salary in lieu of the notice period.

2 Responsibilities During Notice Period

  • Employees must complete proper handover of duties.
  • All Company assets must be returned before the last working day.
  • Employees must cooperate with HR for Full & Final (F&F) settlement.

3. Types of Resignation

A. Resignation with Full Notice Period

  • The employee serves the complete notice period.
  • Resignation must be submitted in writing and through the proper system.
  • The exit process begins before the last working day.
  • HR will complete clearance and conduct an exit interview.
  • Experience letters will be issued after full F&F settlement.

B. Resignation Without Full Notice Period

  • The employee does not serve full notice period.
  • Employees must pay notice pay in lieu of shortfall, unless waived by the Company.
  • Final dues may be adjusted against notice pay where applicable.
  • If notice pay is not paid or waived, an experience letter may not be issued.
  • Legal action may be taken for recovery of dues if required.

4. Exit Formalities

Employees must complete clearance from all departments, including:

  • HR
  • Finance
  • IT
  • Facilities / Operations

They must:

  • Return all Company assets
  • Complete Exit Checklist
  • Attend Exit Interview with HR

Exit feedback may be used for improvement purposes.

5. Leave During Notice Period

  • Employees may use available leave during notice period with approval.
  • If leave is not approved due to work requirements, it may be adjusted or encashed as per Company policy.
  • Leave encashment and waiver together will not be allowed.

6. Performance During Notice Period

  • Poor performance during notice period may lead to warning.
  • If no improvement is seen, the Company may terminate employment.

7. Service Agreement Employees

  • Employees under service agreements must complete the agreed tenure or pay applicable compensation.
  • Non-compliance may lead to legal action and recovery of dues.
  • Final settlement and experience letter may be withheld until resolution.

8. Full & Final Settlement (F&F)

F&F includes:

  • Salary and wage dues
  • Leave encashment
  • Incentives/bonuses (if applicable)
  • PF, gratuity, and statutory benefits
  • Any recoveries (notice pay, damages, etc.)

HR coordinates with Payroll/Finance for final settlement as per applicable laws, including the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972. F&F Settlement will be done within 30 days of the last working day, subject to timely handover subject of work and assets.

  • Employees may request withdrawal of resignation before the last working day.
  • Approval depends on management decisions.

1. Objective

The objective of this Health & Safety Policy is to establish and maintain a safe, healthy, secure, and risk-free working environment for all employees, contractors, visitors, and associated personnel of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. in compliance with applicable safety, labor, environmental, and industrial regulations including the Factories Act, 1948 and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020.

2. Scope

This Health & Safety Policy applies to all employees.

3. Policy

Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. is committed to providing a safe, healthy, secure, and hazard-free workplace for all employees, contractors, visitors, customers, and other persons associated with the Company.

Every employee shares responsibility for maintaining a safe working environment and must follow all safety requirements while performing their duties.

Employee Responsibilities

All employees must:

  • Follow all safety rules, work instructions, operating procedures, emergency guidelines, and Company safety requirements.
  • Use the Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and safety gear provided for their work.
  • Operate machines, tools, or equipment only when properly trained, authorized, and competent to do so.
  • Immediately report any unsafe condition, unsafe act, accident, injury, near miss, equipment malfunction, fire hazard, gas leak, electrical hazard, or other safety concern to their Reporting Manager, Supervisor, Safety Officer, or HR Department.
  • Maintain good housekeeping and keep work areas clean, organized, and free from hazards.
  • Follow approved safety procedures at all times.
  • Participate in safety training programs, toolbox talks, fire drills, mock drills, medical examinations, and other safety awareness activities organized by the Company.
  • Maintain proper hygiene, cleanliness, ergonomics, and safe work practices.
  • Follow both Company safety requirements and customer site safety requirements while working at client locations.

Prohibited Activities

The following are strictly prohibited:

  • Working under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or any intoxicating substance.
  • Smoking, consuming alcohol, or using narcotic substances within Company premises or during official duties.
  • Performing any activity that may endanger people, equipment, property, or business operations.
  • Entering restricted areas without proper authorization or safety precautions.
  • Operating machinery or equipment without approval, training, or competency.

Emergency & Safety Equipment

Employees must ensure that:

  • Emergency exits, evacuation routes, fire extinguishers, hydrants, alarms, first aid boxes, and other emergency equipment remain accessible at all times.
  • Safety signs and emergency systems are not blocked, damaged, or misused.

Environmental & Waste Management

  • Hazardous waste and industrial waste must be handled, stored and disposed of according to environmental and safety requirements.
  • Employees must support environmentally responsible work practices.

Safety Monitoring & Compliance

To maintain a safe workplace, the Company may conduct:

  • Safety inspections
  • Risk assessments
  • Internal audits
  • Equipment inspections
  • Workplace monitoring
  • Health examinations
  • Environmental assessments

Employees are expected to cooperate fully during such activities.

Incident Reporting & Disciplinary Action

Reporting Safety Concerns

  • Every employee must immediately report any safety violation, unsafe condition, or unsafe work practice.
  • Employees may be instructed to stop unsafe work until corrective actions are taken.

Company Authority During Unsafe Conditions

To protect employees, property, equipment, and the environment, the Company may:

  • Stop operations temporarily.
  • Isolate equipment.
  • Restrict access to certain areas.
  • Suspend hazardous activities.
  • Evacuate work locations.
  • Remove personnel from unsafe work situations.

Accident Investigation

All workplace accidents, injuries, incidents, and near misses will be:

  • Recorded,
  • Investigated,
  • Reviewed, and
  • Reported as required by Company procedures and applicable laws.

Non-Compliance

Failure to follow safety requirements may result in disciplinary action.

Depending on the seriousness of the violation, disciplinary action may include:

  • Verbal warning
  • Written warning
  • Safety retraining
  • Suspension from duties
  • Restriction from hazardous work areas
  • Recovery of losses where applicable
  • Termination of employment
  • Any other corrective action considered appropriate by Management

Contractors & Visitors

Contractors, vendors, and other third-party personnel must comply with all Company safety requirements, PPE rules, and site procedures. Failure to do so may result in removal from the site or denial of access.

Legal Compliance

Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. shall comply with all applicable occupational health, safety, environmental, labour welfare, and workplace safety laws, including but not limited to:

  • Factories Act, 1948
  • Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (OSH Code)
  • Employees’ Compensation Act, 1923
  • Environment Protection Act, 1986
  • Applicable Fire Safety Regulations
  • Other applicable statutory requirements issued by Government authorities from time to time

1. Objective

The objective of this Policy is to ensure a fair, structured, and effective recruitment process for selecting qualified, skilled, and suitable candidates for various roles within Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

2. Scope

This Hiring Policy applies to the recruitment and selection of all employees of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

3. Policy

a. Hiring process:

a.1 Whenever a vacancy arises within Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd., the concerned Department Head, Reporting Manager, or authorized supervisor shall identify the manpower requirement and initiate the recruitment process based on operational, technical, administrative, or production needs.

a.2 The concerned department shall submit a duly approved manpower requisition to the HR Department or consultant specifying the position, required qualifications, experience, technical skills, manpower category, and other relevant job requirements for the role.

a.3 The HR Department or consultant may source suitable candidates through internal references, employee referrals, applications on record, job portals, recruitment agencies, campus hiring, technical institutes, walk-in interviews, advertisements, contractors, or any other appropriate recruitment source depending upon the nature of the position. Human Resources obtains qualified candidates and refers them to the supervisor submitting the requisition.

a.4 The HR Department shall coordinate the screening of applications, scheduling of interviews, trade tests, technical evaluations, document verification, reference checks, and other selection procedures in consultation with the concerned department and management.

a.5 Selection of candidates shall be based on qualifications, technical competency, relevant experience, skills, operational suitability, discipline, safety awareness, and organizational requirements in accordance with the Company’s recruitment standards and workforce needs.

a.5.1 Human Resources submits applications and/or resumes of candidates meeting qualifications to the supervisor of the position for review.

a.5.2 If approved by the supervisor, Human Resource schedules interviews for a candidate.

a.6 The selection decision is made by the supervisor from the candidates provided by Human Resources, with the approval of the supervisor’s manager.

a.6.1 Human Resources negotiates starting compensation and dates with the selected candidate and prepares and sends a written offer of employment

a.6.2 When the employment offer is accepted by the selected candidate, Human Resources notifies all other candidates for the position. If the selected candidate declines the offer, the external selection process is continued.

a.7 During the first hours of employment, Human Resources has the employee complete all required documentation process

a.8 When all the process is completed, Human Resources will explain all appropriate conditions of employment and then escort the new employee to the supervisor to whom she/he will report.

b. Rehires: Former employees of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. may be considered for re-employment subject to management approval, provided their previous separation from the Company was voluntary, professional, and in compliance with Company policies including completion of the required notice period, handover formalities, and clearance procedures.

Re-employment shall be based on the employee’s previous performance, conduct, discipline, operational requirements, and suitability for the available position.

The Recruiter will review the personnel file of the former employee who has applied for reemployment and verify eligibility for rehire before forwarding the application. The Hiring Manager will be advised of the former employee's eligibility for rehire and the requirement to check references.

c. Employment of Family Members: Family members or relatives may be employed at Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. provided that such employment does not create any actual or potential conflict of interest, favoritism, supervisory influence, or compromise in professional decision-making. No employee shall have direct reporting authority, performance evaluation responsibility, salary influence, disciplinary control, or employment-related decision-making authority over any immediate family member or close personal relation working within the organization. Employees are required to disclose any such relationship to the HR Department at the time of joining or whenever such relationship arises during employment. The Company reserves the right to take appropriate decisions in order to maintain fairness, transparency, discipline, and operational integrity within the workplace.

d. Confidentiality

  • To protect the privacy of candidates and to preserve the integrity of the recruiting process, all search committee members are required to maintain confidentiality throughout and after the conclusion of the recruitment process.
  • Confidential information includes matters discovered or discussed during the recruiting process.
  • All information relating to the search may only be discussed with other search committee members, Human Services or administrators in the chain of command of the hiring department.
  • Employees who violate this requirement for confidentiality will be subject to corrective or disciplinary action.

c. Equal Employment Opportunity

The aim of the Recruitment and Selection Policy is to ensure that the company select the most suitable person for the job on the basis of their relevant merits and abilities and that no employee/job applicant is unfairly treated on any grounds including Race, Color, Nationality, Ethnic or national origins, Religion, Sex, Sexuality, Actual or perceived Aids/HIV status or perceived association with an HIV positive person, Marital status, Age, Social background or Disability.

c. Complaints of recruitment policy

If any employee/job applicant considers that he or she has been unfairly treated in relation to the recruitment and selection policy, he/she can make a complaint which will be dealt with in accordance with the agreed procedures. This policy is in accordance with the relevant legislation and various codes of practice.

c. Employment categories

Each employee will belong to one other employment category given below:

1. Regular full-time employees

Regular full-time employees are those who are employed on a permanent basis and are regularly scheduled to work the standard working hours of the Company. Such employees may be eligible for Company benefits, allowances, and facilities as per applicable Company policies and employment terms.

2. Part-time employees

Part-time employees are those who are engaged to work for fewer hours than the standard full-time working schedule of the Company. Eligibility for benefits and other facilities shall be governed by Company policy and applicable laws.

3. Probationary employees

Probationary employees are those whose performance, conduct, attendance, discipline, safety compliance, and overall suitability are being evaluated during the probation period prior to confirmation of employment.

4. Contractual employees

Contractual employees are those engaged by the Company for a specific project, assignment, duration, operational requirement, or contractual work under agreed terms and conditions. Their employment shall automatically conclude upon completion of the contract period or assigned work unless otherwise extended by the Company.

5. Trainees / Apprentices

Trainees or apprentices are individuals engaged for training, skill development, industrial exposure, or learning purposes for a specified training period under the guidance of the Company. Their engagement shall not automatically guarantee permanent employment unless specifically confirmed by the management.

6. Temporary / Casual employees

Temporary or casual employees are those engaged for short-term, seasonal, intermittent, urgent, or temporary operational requirements of the Company. Such employment shall remain temporary in nature unless otherwise communicated in writing by the management.

1. Objective

To provide a framework within which reporting managers and HR can work with employees to meet and maintain the high standards of performance and to encourage improvement where necessary.

2. Scope

This policy and procedure applies to all departments and employees of the Organization.

3. Policy

The company aims to ensure that all its employees achieve and maintain high standards of

performance. To that end, company monitors its employees' performance to ensure that these high

standards are being met and maintained; and, where necessary, provide its employees with appropriate

training and support.

  • PIP is applicable to both probationary as well as confirmed candidates.
  • For probationary employees- First review will be within a month of joining and the review period will be of minimum one month or based on the nature of the role and operational requirements. Second review (applicable if first PIP is unsatisfactory) will be after completion of this first review period. In such case second review period will be of minimum one month. Probation period can be extended in case of unsatisfactory performance after applying first PIP. If the employee's reporting manager and HR are not satisfied with the employee's performance, the company may take disciplinary action up to and including the termination of the employee's employment
  • For Confirmed employees- Below PIP Procedure will be followed.
  • Performance shall include productivity, quality of work, technical competency, attendance, behavioural conduct, safety compliance, adherence to Company policies, and achievement of assigned responsibilities.
  • Procedure

Informal Resolution

In some cases, where the reporting manager or HR considers it appropriate, minor performance issues may be dealt with informally.

Formal Resolution

Where performance issues cannot be resolved informally and/or the reporting manager or HR considers such an approach inappropriate, the following two-stage process will be used.

Stage 1 - First Meeting

The employee's reporting manager shall ask HR to initiate the Performance Improvement Process. HR will write to the employee, setting out the areas of concern regarding the employee's performance and arrange a meeting to discuss the matter. The purpose of the First Meeting will be to:

1. Explain the shortfall between the employee's performance and the required standards;

2. Identify any cause or causes of the poor performance;

2. Set objectives and a time frame for the employee to reach the required standards (i.e.the "First Review Period");

3. Outline any additional support and/or training that company will provide the employee during the First Review Period; and

4. Advise the employee of the remaining stages of the process and what may happen if the employee does not achieve the required standard of performance.

5. The Company may provide coaching, mentoring, technical guidance, retraining, supervisory support, or skill development interventions wherever considered appropriate.

The employee's reporting manager and HR will monitor the employee's performance during the First Review Period. At the end of the First Review Period, HR will write to the employee to inform him/her of the outcome:

  • If the employee's reporting manager and HR are satisfied with the employee's performance, no further action will be taken; or
  • If the employee's reporting manager and HR are not satisfied with the employee's performance, the matter will be progressed to Stage 2.

Stage 2 - Second Meeting

If no, or insufficient, improvement is achieved during the First Review Period, HR will request that the employee attend a Second Meeting to discuss this. The Second Meeting will consider:

1. The employee's performance to date;

2. What steps the employee has/has not taken to improve his/her performance;

3. Whether there is a reasonable prospect for improvement in the employee's performance (so as to reach the required standard); and

4. What action is considered appropriate in the circumstances?

At the Second Meeting the employee may be given a further opportunity to improve his/her performance within a second specified timeframe (the "Second Review Period"). If so, the employee's reporting manager and HR will continue to monitor the employee's performance during the Second Review Period. At the end of the Second Review Period, HR will write to the employee to inform him/her of the outcome:

  • If the employee's reporting manager and HR are satisfied with the employee's performance, no further action will be taken; or
  • If the employee's reporting manager and HR are not satisfied with the employee's performance, Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. may take disciplinary action up to and including the termination of the employee's employment.
  • All PIP discussions, objectives, review findings, feedback, improvement plans, and outcomes shall be documented and maintained in the employee's personnel records.
  • This policy shall be administered in accordance with applicable labor laws, employment regulations, and Company policies.

Alternatively, the company may decide at the Second Meeting itself to take disciplinary action up to and including the termination of the employee's employment. The company reserves the right to decide, in its absolute discretion, which of the mentioned courses of action it will follow, or to take such other action as it deems appropriate in the circumstances.

Visitors include customers, vendors, contractors, consultants, auditors, inspectors, job applicants, transport personnel, service providers, government officials, and any other non-employees entering the premises for official or business purposes.

Entry Requirements and Registration

All visitors must comply with the Company’s entry and security procedures. They are required to register at the security gate, provide valid identification, share their purpose of visit, and follow all access control instructions. After registration, visitors will be issued a visitor pass or identification badge, which must be worn/displayed at all times inside the premises.

Access and Movement Restrictions

Visitors shall be allowed entry only for approved business purposes such as meetings, inspections, audits, deliveries, or service-related work. Movement within the premises shall be restricted to authorized areas only. Entry into production areas, stores, electrical rooms, or any restricted or safety-sensitive zones is strictly prohibited unless properly authorized and supervised.

Safety Requirements

Visitors entering factory or operational areas must comply with all safety rules, including wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) wherever required. The employee hosting the visitor is responsible for ensuring that all safety and operational guidelines are followed during the visit.

Security and Confidentiality

Visitors are strictly prohibited from photographing, recording, copying, or sharing any Company-related confidential information, processes, equipment, or documents without written approval. Carrying weapons, alcohol, drugs, hazardous materials, or any prohibited items inside the premises is not allowed.

Inspection and Monitoring

The Company may conduct security checks of bags, vehicles and belongings at entry and exit points. CCTV surveillance, access control systems, and other monitoring tools may be used to ensure safety and security of the premises, employees, and assets.

Conduct and Responsibility

All visitors must maintain proper discipline and follow instructions given by security personnel and Company staff. Employees hosting visitors are responsible for ensuring compliance with all safety, security, and operational rules during the visit.

Right to Refuse Entry

The Company reserves the right to deny entry, restrict access, or remove any visitor from the premises at any time if they violate rules or pose a risk to safety, security, or operations.

Parking Policy

  • Parking facilities are provided solely for official and authorized use by employees, visitors, and company vehicles.
  • Employees must park their vehicles only in designated parking areas as allotted by the management.
  • Vehicles must be parked in a disciplined and orderly manner without obstructing entrances, exits, pathways, emergency routes, or operational areas.
  • Rash driving, honking, speeding, or unsafe movement of vehicles within the premises is strictly prohibited.
  • The company shall not be responsible for any loss, theft, or damage to vehicles or personal belongings parked on company premises.
  • Unauthorized parking or misuse of parking facilities will be treated as misconduct and may invite disciplinary action.
  • Management reserves the right to regulate, modify, or withdraw parking facilities at its discretion based on operational or safety requirements

Non-Compliance

Any violation of this policy, including unauthorized entry, misuse of visitor passes, restricted area access, unauthorized recording, or misconduct, may result in removal from the premises, restriction of future access, disciplinary action, or legal action as deemed appropriate by the Company.

3. Exceptions

All exceptions and deviations to this policy will require the approval of all the directors.

3. Effective Date

This policy will come into effect from 30th June 2026. The Company reserves the right to review, interpret, modify, or amend this policy in accordance with legal, operational, and compliance requirements.

policy_name: Work from home/ Remote Work Policy
content:
1. Objective

The objective of this Work from Home / Remote Work Policy is to establish clear guidelines for eligible employees working remotely while ensuring productivity, accountability, operational continuity, communication efficiency, data confidentiality, and compliance with Company requirements. The policy aims to provide workplace flexibility for suitable roles without affecting the operational, manufacturing, technical, and business requirements of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd.

2. Scope

This Work from Home / Remote Work Policy applies to eligible employees of Thermo Heat Transfers Pvt. Ltd. whose job responsibilities can be effectively performed outside the Company premises.

3. Policy

  • Work From Home may be allowed only for roles that can be performed remotely without affecting productivity, communication, confidentiality, safety, or business operations.
  • Employees in manufacturing, production, machine operations, maintenance, fabrication, shop-floor, quality inspection, and similar roles are generally not eligible unless specially approved by management.
  • Eligibility depends on job nature, performance, discipline, communication, and business requirements.

1. Approval Requirement

  • Prior written approval from the Reporting Manager, Department Head, or HR is mandatory before working from home.
  • Emergency or special cases must also be approved by management.

2. Types of WFH

Work From Home may be granted as:

  • Temporary arrangement
  • Occasional or hybrid work
  • Project-based work
  • Emergency or medical need
  • Business continuity requirement

3. Working Hours & Availability

  • Employees must remain available during official working hours.
  • Regular communication must be maintained with managers, team members, and stakeholders.
  • Attendance in meetings, calls, and reviews is mandatory.

4. Performance & Discipline

  • Employees must maintain the same level of productivity and discipline as in office work.
  • Timely completion of tasks and responsiveness is required.
  • Work From Home is not a substitute for leave or reduced working responsibility.

5. Data Security & Confidentiality

  • Company data, documents, drawings, systems, and confidential information must be protected at all times.
  • Company devices, software, email, and systems must be used only for official work.
  • Sharing of confidential information without approval is strictly prohibited.

6. Work Environment

  • Employees must ensure a safe, professional, and distraction-free workspace while working remotely.

7. Reporting & Monitoring

  • Employees may be required to submit reports, task updates, and work progress regularly.
  • Attendance, login/logout, productivity, and performance may be monitored by the Company.

8. Office Visit Requirement

  • Employees working from home may be required to report to the office, plant, or client location whenever required by management.

9. Withdrawal of WFH

The Company may withdraw or cancel Work From Home at any time due to:

  • Operational requirements
  • Poor performance or discipline issues
  • Communication gaps
  • Confidentiality or security concerns
  • Business needs

10. Non-Compliance & Disciplinary Action

  • Violations of WFH rules may result in disciplinary action.
  • Confidentiality breaches or misuse of remote work privileges will be treated as serious misconduct.
  • Possible actions include:
  • Warning (verbal/written)
  • Withdrawal of WFH privileges
  • Performance review
  • Suspension
  • Salary recovery (if applicable)
  • Termination of employment

3. Exceptions

All exceptions and deviations to this policy will require the approval of all the directors.

3. Effective Date

This policy will come into effect from 30th June 2026. The Company reserves the right to review, interpret, modify, or amend this policy in accordance with legal, operational, and compliance requirements.
